prompt: Exactly $50\%$ of the students at a large university have part-time jobs. A random sample of $400$ students is taken. What is the probability that the sample proportion with jobs is $0.55$ or higher? Use $P(Z \ge 0.1) = 0.4602$, $P(Z \ge 1) = 0.1587$, $P(Z \ge 2) = 0.0228$. Round to four decimal places.
hint: Find the SD of $\hat{p}$ first: $\sqrt{p(1-p)/n}$. Then standardize $0.55$.

hints.text: Find the SD of $\hat{p}$ first: $\sqrt{p(1-p)/n}$. Then standardize $0.55$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: with $p = 0.5$ and $n = 100$, $\sigma_{\hat{p}} = \sqrt{0.25/100} = 0.05$. Here $n = 400$ makes it smaller.

explanation: Large Counts: $np = 200$ and $n(1-p) = 200$, both $\ge 10$, so $\hat{p}$ is approximately normal with mean $0.5$ and SD $\sqrt{(0.5)(0.5)/400} = \sqrt{0.000625} = 0.025$.
$P(Z \ge 2) = 0.0228$. A sample proportion of $0.55$ or more would happen only about $2\%$ of the time.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think in counts
steps: $\hat{p} \ge 0.55$ means at least $0.55 \times 400 = 220$ students with jobs.
The count is binomial with mean $200$ and SD $\sqrt{400(0.5)(0.5)} = 10$.
$220$ is $2$ SDs above $200$, so $z = 2$ and the probability is $0.0228$.
